title: The Wazir of al-Yaman and His Younger Brother

keywords: the wazir of al-yaman and his younger brother
full_text:
In the ancient kingdom of Yemen, King As'ad had for his Grand Vizier a statesman of extraordinary wisdom named Mansur. Mansur governed the kingdom with such equity, expanding agriculture, constructing cisterns, and establishing fair markets, that the realm flourished in unprecedented prosperity.

Mansur had a younger brother named Haydar, whom he loved with boundless affection. Rather than keeping all royal honors to himself, Mansur petitioned the king: 'Sire, power is a heavy mantle that bends the back of a single man. My brother Haydar is endowed with courage, intellect, and an upright heart. Let him share the vizierate with me, that two hands may uphold your throne.'

The king consented, and the two brothers sat side by side in the council hall, dividing the duties of state: Mansur directed the civil administration and the courts of justice, while Haydar organized the frontiers and commanded the armed defenses.

Jealous courtiers, unable to comprehend such fraternal unity, sought to sow discord between them. One courtier crept to Haydar, whispering: 'Your brother treats you as a subordinate; he keeps the royal treasury in his palace and gives you only the dusty labor of the camps.' Another courtier whispered to Mansur: 'Beware of Haydar; his soldiers revere him, and he plots to usurp your seat.'

The two brothers listened with serene composure, and that evening, met in their father’s ancestral garden.

Mansur embraced Haydar, and Haydar embraced Mansur. They recounted to each other every word the slanderers had whispered, laughing at the transparent malice of the courtiers.

The next morning before the assembled court, Mansur presented Haydar with the keys to the treasury, and Haydar placed the command sword into Mansur's hands, demonstrating before all men that fraternal trust is a citadel that slander cannot breach. The king banished the envious conspirators and ruled in peace for forty years, supported by the twin pillars of brotherhood.
moral: Fraternal love that shares power and wealth without envy creates an unshakeable fortress for an empire.
